items.name: LLM Wiki
items.description: crow-hq/llm-wiki-v2: a markdown wiki the agents ingest external material into (specs, notes, papers). Runs as a separate process because it is AGPL.

items.name: Laya
items.description: NandhaKishorM/laya, always-on extension the agents can call from within a quest.

items.name: ComfyUI
items.description: comfyanonymous/ComfyUI: node-graph image generation on the runtime's GPU (FLUX.1 schnell by default). Starts by itself where there is an NVIDIA GPU (a RunPod GPU pod); COMFYUI=1 starts it anywhere, COMFYUI_URL uses one that runs elsewhere.

items.name: Video
items.description: Text-to-video and image-to-video on the ComfyUI arm: Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B (Apache-2.0, 1280x704 at 24 fps, ~18 GB) by default, LTX-Video 2B distilled (~11.5 GB) for fast drafts. Weights are fetched onto the volume the first time each model is asked for. Needs the GPU pod.

items.name: Qwen-Image
items.description: Sketch to image, edits by instruction and repainting inside a mask on the ComfyUI arm, with Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 (Apache-2.0, fp8, ~31 GB with its encoder and the 4-step Lightning LoRA). Weights are fetched onto the volume the first time a tool needs them. Needs the GPU pod.

items.name: SAM 3
items.description: Masks and cutouts from words, points or a box on the ComfyUI arm, with SAM 3.1 (Meta's SAM License, ~1.7 GB) through ComfyUI's own SAM3_Detect node. Fetched on first use. Needs the GPU pod.

items.name: Upscale and cleanup
items.description: Real-ESRGAN (x4, x4 anime, x2) and HAT (real-world x4) upscaling through spandrel, and background removal through rembg (IS-Net, BiRefNet, U2-Net). Its own process on :7339; CUDA on the GPU pod, Apple's GPU on a Mac, the CPU anywhere else. Weights are fetched on first use.

items.name: Unlimited-OCR
items.description: baidu/Unlimited-OCR (huggingface.co/baidu/Unlimited-OCR, MIT, 3B): reads scans, photos of pages and PDFs into markdown on the runtime's GPU. Starts by itself where there is an NVIDIA GPU (the GPU pod) and sleeps elsewhere; OCR_URL uses one that runs on another machine.

items.name: Claude wisps (cloud)
items.description: Claude Code cloud sessions (claude.ai/code) as a kind of wisp: wisp_send with where "claude" hands one a self-contained task through a routine's API trigger; they work on Anthropic's machines on Felipe's subscription while the Mac sleeps and come back as draft pull requests. Needs CLAUDE_ROUTINE_URL and CLAUDE_ROUTINE_TOKEN in the key vault (forge/wisps/README.md).

items.name: Docling (documents)
items.description: docling-project/docling (MIT): turns PDFs, scans, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML and images into clean Markdown with tables and reading order, for the agents, the LLM Wiki and the brain. Runs on CPU on the Mac and on a RunPod pod; its own OCR reads scans, and the Unlimited-OCR arm takes over thin scans when it is up.

items.name: draw.io (diagrams)
items.description: jgraph/drawio-mcp (Apache-2.0, @drawio/mcp 1.7.0) with draw.io Desktop's command line: Mermaid, CSV or draw.io XML become an editable .drawio diagram, laid out with ELK when asked, exported as SVG, PNG or PDF, and the shape library (over 10,000 shapes) can be searched. The MCP runs behind a loopback HTTP server, with no browser and no shell; CPU only, no key.

items.name: D2 (diagrams from text)
items.description: d2lang/d2 (MPL-2.0, v0.9.0, a pinned and checksum-verified binary) with its bundled TALA layout (open source and in the same binary since 0.9.0, no plugin and no licence key): D2 text becomes a clean, repeatable SVG, PNG or PDF with orthogonal edge routing, laid out by TALA, ELK or dagre, and the source can be validated with line numbers. A loopback Node server runs d2 with an argument list and a clean environment, kills it after its own timeout and caps the source size. CPU only, no key. Off until the owner switches it on.

items.name: DuckDB (data)
items.description: duckdb/duckdb (MIT, duckdb 1.5.6 from PyPI): read-only SQL over the project's CSV, Parquet, JSON and Excel files, and a file's schema, row count and sample. A loopback Python server opens a fresh in-memory connection per query, lets it read only the project's own files, accepts one SELECT, WITH, DESCRIBE, SUMMARIZE or SHOW statement classified by DuckDB's own parser, and caps rows, memory and time. CPU only, no key; the Excel extension is installed once and nothing else is loaded.

items.name: Scraper (references)
items.description: References for the generative arms, gathered from the web: yt-dlp (Unlicense, 2026.8.19) for video and sound from over a thousand sites, cut to a time range; gallery-dl (GPL-2.0, 1.32.16, run as its own command) for galleries and boards on 300+ sites; a page pass over og:image, img, srcset, picture and video tags, with the browser arm for pages built by JavaScript; and Openverse and Wikimedia Commons searched by words for openly licensed pictures and clips. Every file lands in the file store with its page, author and licence. A loopback Python server fetches only public http(s) sites, honours robots.txt, pauses between requests and caps files, sizes and time. CPU only, no key.

items.name: REA (reverse engineering)
items.description: morluto/rea (MIT, rea-agents 6.5.0), run as its own command behind a loopback server: a file or folder of the project is read, never run. JavaScript and Electron apps (modules, imports, IPC), .NET assemblies (types, methods, CIL, strings), Go and Rust binaries, ELF, Mach-O and PE files, APKs, Flutter builds, firmware, WASM, EVM bytecode, SQLite files and pcaps. Every result says what it could not see, and the full Evidence is kept in a file to page through. Native decompiling through Hopper, Ghidra or IDA is not wired in. CPU only, no key.

items.name: doop (design canvases)
items.description: kgoedecke/doop (AGPL-3.0, 0.8.0 at b5ab860a), the open alternative to Paper: design canvases whose frames are real HTML and CSS, edited by people in the browser and by the agents through doop's own tool server. Run unmodified as its own process behind a loopback server (cloned and built with bun into .hephaestus/arms/doop, never into this repository), with one local account the agents and the owner share; every frame an agent makes or changes comes back as a picture and is kept in the project with its HTML. Frame pictures need Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave. CPU only, no key; doop's own built-in agent stays off.

items.name: OpenCut (video edits)
items.description: opencut-app/opencut (MIT), the open browser video editor, and FFmpeg (LGPL/GPL, run as a separate program, never linked or bundled): cut_probe reads a clip's length, size, rotation, frame rate, codecs and loudness; cut_edit renders a timeline headless on FFmpeg (trims, crop or reframe to 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1, speed, crossfades and other xfade transitions, titles and SRT captions through libass, a music bed ducked under speech, -14 LUFS) into an MP4 in .hephaestus/uploads; cut_open gathers the media and the timeline into a folder with the OpenCut link for hand-tuning; cut_frame takes one frame of a clip as a picture (its last frame starts the next generated clip). The skill opencut:video-editor is the editor's method: cutting, stitching generated clips into one flow, sound, titles, and showing the cut on the owner's timeline. OpenCut's own headless renderer, Editor API and MCP are announced, not shipped, so FFmpeg is the engine until they are. A library arm on the CPU: ready when an ffmpeg answers (Homebrew's ffmpeg-full on a Mac for titles and captions); no key, nothing downloaded.

items.name: Workbench (media to the workspaces)
items.description: The hands between the city's media and the workspaces, written for Hephaestus. media_find finds the clips, sounds, pictures and meshes the agents made and the owner dropped in (the gallery's list), newest first, by kind, words, quest or arm, each with its gallery id, the path to hand to any arm, its length and size and what made it. workspace_show puts work in front of the owner while it is made: a cut_edit timeline laid on the cutting room's timeline as a draft (offered instead when the owner has a cut of their own), a picture on the light table, a clip on the monitor, a mesh on the casting floor, a storyboard on the board wall. A library arm in the runtime: no process, no port, no key, always ready.

items.name: Director (storyboards)
items.description: The storyboard director, art director and producer for the generative arms, written for Hephaestus from the method of several open storyboard skills (credited in docs/arms/director.md; no code or text copied). A storyboard is one file the owner edits in the storyboard editor and the agents write through the tools: brief, style bible, characters, places and props declared once, a Fountain script, scenes and shots with their size, angle, move, lens, aperture, light and length, the takes each arm made, and the audio. film_grammar is the vocabulary (21 visual styles; 86 shot sizes, angles, moves, lenses and apertures; lighting, composition, transitions, grades, story structures, formats and craft rules) with every engine's real limits; board_sketches reads the owner's sketches (a sheet is cut into panels) onto shots; board_save writes and reviews; board_plan prices the shots as arm calls and spends nothing; board_attach files each result as a take; board_cut cuts the picked takes, or an animatic of stills, through the OpenCut arm's engine. The skill director:storyboard-director is the method. A library arm on the CPU: no process, no port, no key; ffmpeg for panels, stills and the cut.

items.name: Companion (chibi gods)
items.description: The desktop companion: a chibi girl for each god of the themes (Hephaestus, Artemisa, Zeus, Poseidon, Apollo) who sits at her desk on the owner's desktop while the app is minimised or in the background, follows the pointer, types while the agents work, reacts to the forge's moments (a quest starting, a bug caught and eaten, something forged, a quest failing, the owner's word needed) and opens the running projects, their arms and chats when clicked. Each god is a puppet the forge drew with its own arms: a master picture cut out of its paper, the regions her mesh bends by, and small sprites for each expression (eyes closed, half, happy, wide, winking, sparkling, hearts; mouth open, o, smile, pout; a blush, a sweat drop, a lifted paw, her attribute raised). companion_look shows one, companion_tune changes her motion, expressions, moments and lines, companion_say puts a line in her bubble, companion_part turns an image arm's edit of her into a new or redrawn sprite, companion_make rigs a new god from one picture. Settings, Companion is the owner's editor. A library arm in the runtime: no process, no port, no key, no package; the owner's changes live in ~/.hephaestus/companions.

items.name: RAG-Anything
items.description: HKUDS/RAG-Anything (github.com/HKUDS/RAG-Anything, MIT, raganything 1.4.2 from PyPI) on LightRAG: the forge's multimodal retrieval layer. The brain's docs, what Unlimited-OCR and Docling read and what a spider adds go in as text, tables, equations and images, become a knowledge graph plus vectors, and rag_ask answers across them with sources. Runs on the CPU; its model is Claude through the runtime (or an OpenAI-compatible one), its embeddings are made locally with fastembed.

items.name: Leviathan
items.description: elstongun/leviathan (github.com/elstongun/leviathan, Apache-2.0, the v0.2.0 release binary pinned by checksum): the forge's long-term memory. One claim per memory under a subject and a key; a new value for the same key replaces the old one and keeps it as history; recall is ranked full-text search inside a token budget, and every quest starts with its briefing. Each memory is written in the namespace of the person whose spiders learned it, with the species as its source. No model runs inside it, and secrets are refused. The store lives on the host; brain/memory/memories.jsonl is its copy in git, written by one host at a time.

items.name: Browser (Playwright)
items.description: microsoft/playwright (Apache-2.0): a headless Chromium the spiders drive to browse, scrape and test pages, the live app included, without anyone's own browser. Screenshots land on the Loom. Runs on CPU on the Mac and on a RunPod pod.

items.name: Local model
items.description: A small open model (qwen3:4b, with qwen3-embedding:0.6b for embeddings) served by Ollama on this machine for the cheap bulk work: tagging, summarising, classifying, ranking. Free; on the GPU pod it lets go of the card when idle. Also serves the models the training arm makes.

items.name: Training (Unsloth)
items.description: Fine-tunes small open models with LoRA on the project's own data: Unsloth on the GPU pod (4-bit, exports a GGUF the local model serves), Transformers + PEFT on a Mac. Runs survive the pod sleeping and resume from their last checkpoint; an agent can only propose one, the owner approves it in the app.

items.name: Whisper (the ears)
items.description: SYSTRAN/faster-whisper: speech to text on the runtime, the small model in int8 on a laptop CPU and large-v3-turbo on a GPU. The app's mic sends voice notes here, and the agents transcribe recordings with it.

items.name: Kokoro (the voice)
items.description: hexgrad/Kokoro-82M through thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx (Apache-2.0): text to speech on the CPU, 54 voices in nine languages. Reads Hephaestus's answers aloud in the app and gives the agents a speak tool.

items.name: 3D Magic Caster
items.description: The 3D arm: felipelopezm1/3D-Magic-Caster brought into the forge. An ask or an image becomes a mesh with free models ComfyUI runs on the GPU (TRELLIS.2 textured PBR by default, MIT; Hunyuan3D 2.1 when asked), finished as GLB, OBJ or FBX (Blender's bpy). Starts by itself where there is an NVIDIA GPU (the GPU pod) and sleeps elsewhere; COMFYUI_URL points it at a ComfyUI on another machine. The checkout is the original wizard, readable with forge_docs.

items.name: Code-as-World
items.description: mirros-lab/code-as-world (Apache-2.0): physics as executable code. world_simulate runs a world the agents write (scene.json + scene.xml) in MuJoCo on any CPU and returns its trajectory and a video; world_measure asks Code-as-World-VL (4B or 9B) a quantitative question about a video on the GPU pod. CODEWORLD_URL uses one that runs on another machine.

items.name: Anatomy (figures)
items.description: wheresryan22/anatomy (MIT): a skill that explains an idea by drawing it as a real, working machine in isometric SVG (with optional WebGL and 3D layers), handed to the spiders as anatomy:anatomy, plus a renderer that films what they build, or any SVG or HTML diagram, in headless Chromium: a poster, a standalone SVG and a WebM or MP4 (GIF and animated SVG on request) the Loom plays, scrubs and saves. Runs on CPU on the Mac and on a RunPod pod.

items.name: pen.dev (designs)
items.description: pen.dev (formerly Pencil, by High Agency): a design canvas whose .pen files are open JSON (frames with flex layout, text, shapes, icons, variables, components). Its CLI (@pen.dev/cli, proprietary, installed from npm on first start and never bundled) runs the same editor headless: its own agent designs screens, pages and slides from a brief, execute snippets edit a design precisely, and exports give PNG, PDF or HTML with Tailwind to build from. With the pen.dev app open on the Mac, edits land in it live. Needs a pen.dev sign-in on the machine (pen login, or PEN_CLI_KEY). The code editor opens .pen files in a Design tab.

items.name: Tisa
items.description: felipelopezm1/Tisa: the forge's feature and context platform. Online and offline queries with their explanations, the feature graph and its lineage, plans, parity, benches, and a review of a branch against main. Deploying a project folder to a branch waits for a yes. The Python engine is cloned into .hephaestus/arms/tisa and served on loopback. No model of its own, so each runtime on a Mac starts its own, on a port taken from the runtime's port.

items.name: AI Research Skills
items.description: Orchestra-Research/AI-Research-SKILLs: a library of research skills loaded into the forge as Claude Code skills.

items.name: Helix Foundry
items.description: HelixDB/helix-foundry: fundamentals for decoding and reverse engineering ideas into new projects, diagrams and flows.

items.name: Sketch Realistic (image maker)
items.description: felipelopezm1/sketch-realistic: the image and html maker of Hephaestus. Needs its API key as an environment variable, never in git.

items.name: Cursor wisps (local)
items.description: Cursor's AI agents hired as wisps: the Cursor CLI (cursor.com/docs/cli) on this machine, signed in with the owner's Cursor login, takes a task from a spider and works in the project folder or its own worktree. forge/arms/cursor/setup.sh installs it and signs in.

items.name: Cursor wisps (cloud)
items.description: Cursor's Cloud Agents API (cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api): wisps that run on Cursor's machines against the project's GitHub repo, push a cursor/... branch and can open a pull request, and keep going while this machine sleeps. Needs CURSOR_API_KEY in the key vault.

items.name: AI Engineering From Scratch
items.description: rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch: the tongs of the forge, training models from scratch.

items.name: Treasure-hunt quests
items.description: Quest format inspired by boat.dev: a goal, clues, milestones and a treasure that lands in the armory.
